sources.title: 10 December 2021 appointment report and biographical dates
sources.findings: Read the 10 December 2021 appointment and biographical paragraphs. They report the same-day presidential appointment, replacement of Christophe Dabire, 10 October 1963 birth and Paris XI geophysics doctorate. Much of the biography links to translated Wikipedia and is not independent primary authentication. The current-executive-secretary wording was already stale by December 2021; do not copy it. Exact birth date is corroborated by search-indexed Actualite and OCLC entries, whose full relevant bodies were unavailable, not by a civil register. Avoid unverified birth-place precision. Degree year 1993 is not retained publicly because other read CVs give 1992.

sources.title: Biographical education, mining career, IDC and scientific-data work
sources.findings: Read the short WEF biography: Paris XI geophysics doctorate listed as 1993, BHP then Anglo American, and International Data Centre directorship 2004–2013. Its since-2013 executive-secretary heading is historical, not proof of current office. It describes scientific conferences, tsunami-warning cooperation and the virtual Data Exploitation Centre. Public text does not conflate responsibility for a data centre with founding the entire monitoring system. The BHP starting-year detail conflicts with the more detailed RTB/Sidwaya CV and is omitted.

sources.title: Geophysics doctorate and monitoring/science-diplomacy biography
sources.findings: Read the ELN education and career paragraphs: Burkinabe nationality, Paris XI geophysics PhD in 1993, earlier IDC leadership and monitoring assistance relating to DPRK tests, Fukushima and tsunami warnings. The profile still presents him as incumbent CTBTO head and includes 2013 conference responsibilities; it is used for historical career, not November 2026 office. No doctorate certificate or thesis was accessed. Public degree year is omitted because read national CVs disagree.

sources.title: Appointment report and detailed CV, including conflicting degree years and office chronology
sources.findings: Read the Sidwaya education and detailed-career excerpts. The article itself is internally inconsistent: narrative says doctorate in 1993, appended CV says 1992. Public text states the degree and institution without choosing a year by majority vote. CV gives IDC November 2004–July 2013, executive secretary 1 August 2013–31 July 2021, emeritus in July 2021 and Rwanda board chair from October 2021. Therefore the Rwanda chairmanship was not necessarily first obtained after the January 2022 coup. No exact first board-appointment decree was reviewed. Retain only the year 2004 for IDC entry, and no exact BHP joining year. Promotional claims and honorary titles are not substituted for earned degrees.

sources.title: Official Secretariat history and 2013/2021 succession dates
sources.findings: Read the CTBTO official Provisional Technical Secretariat history. It explicitly gives Zerbo as third executive secretary from 1 August 2013 and Robert Floyd as fourth from 1 August 2021. The executive secretary is appointed by and reports to the Preparatory Commission. This is not UN secretary-general or leadership of an already fully operational post-entry-into-force treaty organization. The Secretariat page was accessible even though several separate historical CTBTO news pages returned 403.

sources.title: Treaty, Preparatory Commission and entry-into-force conditions
sources.findings: Read the official treaty overview, including the 1996 Preparatory Commission resolution, present non-entry-into-force statement, and Article XIV/Annex 2 requirements. Distinguish a functioning preparatory monitoring system from entry into force of the CTBT and its eventual legal verification regime. Do not claim Zerbo achieved universal ratification, the treaty entered into force, or an on-site exercise was an authorized inspection of an actual nuclear test.

sources.title: Nature’s 10 (2017): Lassina Zerbo and nuclear-test monitoring
sources.findings: Read the Lassina Zerbo section of Nature’s 2017 annual feature, not every other profile. It describes the 3 September DPRK test, his exchanges with diplomats, the international monitoring network, scientific data sharing and treaty advocacy. His comments and outside praise are attributed perspectives, not a quantified causal evaluation. Nature’s 10 is an editorial personalities feature, not a Nobel Prize or a research degree. Older station counts and geopolitical statements are not used as current 2026 figures.

sources.publisher: Burkina Faso Ministry of Communication / RTB
sources.title: Government review: 10 December 2021 appointment and 13 December cabinet formation
sources.findings: Read the relevant pages of the government bimonthly review hosted by RTB: appointment on 10 December 2021, new government formed on 13 December and security/state-authority priorities. Appointment, formation and parliamentary investiture are separate events. The review’s cabinet-size description differs from Anadolu’s counting; public text omits the count rather than silently treating different inclusion conventions as identical. Government advocacy and operational security claims in other sections were not independently audited or adopted.

sources.title: 7 January 2022 general policy declaration: four priorities
sources.findings: Read the cover, opening and four-priority section of the 7 January 2022 general policy declaration, plus relevant governance paragraphs. It prioritizes peace/security and resilience, return of internally displaced people, reconciliation, and anti-corruption/illicit-enrichment work. The published document says only the delivered speech is authoritative; no audio/video comparison was performed. Commitments in a policy address are not demonstrated outcomes. This PDF is not itself the parliamentary voting record.

sources.title: 8 January report of the previous evening’s parliamentary investiture vote
sources.findings: Read Anadolu’s 8 January 2022 retrospective report of the Friday evening investiture: 103 yes, 24 abstentions, zero no out of 127. Pair with the 7 January dated policy declaration to establish event day, rather than using next-day publication. The report incorrectly calls him 59, inconsistent with the reported October 1963 birth at that date; no age is copied. Its physicist shorthand is rendered as geophysicist using the educational biographies. Not a new first appointment on 7 or 8 January.

sources.title: 24 January 2022 coup and dissolution of government and parliament
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ 24 January 2022 opening and relevant coup paragraphs via Investing.com: army ousted President Kabore and announced suspension of the constitution and dissolution of government/parliament. The military’s justification is its account, not independent endorsement or democratic authorization. Contemporaneous uncertainty about Kabore’s location or detention is not evidence that Zerbo personally was held in the same circumstances. Public text does not adopt unverified arrest/release detail or confuse this coup with the later September 2022 coup.

sources.title: 28 August 2024 Presidential Order 071/01: energy-adviser appointment effective from 22 May
sources.findings: Read Presidential Order 071/01 in the 28 August 2024 special Official Gazette, especially English/French appointment and Article 4 (printed pages 62–64). It appoints Zerbo energy adviser and member of the Strategy and Policy Council in the Office of the President. The order enters into force on gazette publication and takes effect from 22 May 2024, the cited cabinet decision. Public timeline uses the effect date and explains later publication; neither is treated as the first Rwanda board chairmanship. Read those provisions only, not all 7825 extracted lines or the Kinyarwanda legal text.

sources.title: Current board: chairman and presidential energy adviser
sources.findings: Read the Rwanda Atomic Energy Board board page. It names Zerbo energy adviser to the President and chairman, and separately lists Fidele Ndahao as CEO. This confirms institutional distinction rather than making Zerbo CEO or a Rwandan national. The page has an internally awkward sentence about serving within the organization before joining it; that wording is not copied. Generic praise is not independent evaluation of nuclear safety or programme success.

sources.title: 30 June 2026 release on completed joint coordination meeting and SMR roadmap
sources.findings: Read the 30 June 2026 Rosatom/Atom Media release describing the completed Moscow Joint Coordinating Committee meeting, co-chairing with Kirill Komarov, SMR roadmap and workforce/regulatory/scientific cooperation. The release is a participant’s account. It supports a June event with contemporary WNN reporting; no exact meeting day is inferred from publication. The research-reactor proposal and early-2030s nuclear-power aspiration are plans, not proof of licensed construction, financing completion or operation.

sources.title: 1 July 2026 report on completed meeting and Rwanda’s future nuclear-energy plans
sources.findings: Read the opening and quoted planning sections of WNN’s 1 July 2026 report. It describes the coordination meeting and roadmap as completed, supporting June rather than the contradictory July dateline in a Rwanda-government repost. WNN is a nuclear-industry publication using participant information, not an independent regulator’s project certification. The read section describes future plans; no reactor has been declared operational on that basis.

sources.title: 1 November 2026 retrospective on Zerbo’s 28 October Moscow panel
sources.findings: Read Rwanda Inspirer’s 1 November 2026 report of the 28 October Moscow panel during the third Russia–Africa Summit business programme. It reports completed moderation by Zerbo as RAEB chairman/presidential adviser and substantive discussion of training, infrastructure and cooperation. This supports recent life/activity and current roles; 1 November is publication, not event day. The article is closely aligned with Rosatom communications, so industry promotion, Africa-wide construction rhetoric and future targets are not independent evidence of a functioning Rwanda reactor. The retrospective explicitly locates the first joint committee meeting in June 2026.
